observations: alloc_workqueue returns an allocated workqueue pointer or NULL
destroy_workqueue is a separate teardown API
destroy_workqueue unregisters the queue and drains pending work before releasing it

locations: entire aw_remove body; no load of state+0x448 and no destroy_workqueue relocation

observations: destroy_workqueue direct import and call count 0
workqueue pointer identity/path relations were previously left open
trace allocation pointer, consumers, and teardown ordering before concluding release status

whole_stock_assembly_search.interpretation: The stock assembly export has one direct allocation relocation and no direct destroy_workqueue relocation. The indirect-call audit remains incomplete globally.

finding.title: probe-created per-device workqueue is not released by stock remove
finding.impact: On a successful probe followed by unbind, the workqueue object and its worker resources can remain allocated after the devm state containing the only observed handle is released.

limits: The conclusion combines the exact allocation/store, full aw_remove body, whole stock assembly search, target API contract, and raw pointer references; it is not based on an API count alone.
The whole-module indirect-call target audit remains incomplete; the report makes no claim about unobserved arbitrary indirect targets beyond the reviewed stock relocations and state references.
No code was changed and no Docker rebuild was run for this read-only review.
hardening_follow_up: First prevent new submissions and drain every work item that uses the queue, including the Richtap item at state+0x668 and asynchronous firmware producers.
Then call destroy_workqueue on the stored state+0x448 pointer before devres releases the state, and clear the stored pointer if lifecycle permits reuse.
Revalidate probe failure paths as well as normal unbind against the canonical Docker kernel build.
